ai.title: Help banner gains Tips section with conditional OAuth prompt
ai.summary: cli/src/components/help-banner.tsx adds a Tips section to the CLI help banner. Includes a conditional prompt to run /connect for /plan and /review access when Freebuff mode is active and ChatGPT OAuth is disconnected. Static tips cover @ file/agent references and Esc for response cancellation.

eli5.text: When you open the help screen in the command-line version of the assistant, you will now see a small Tips area near the bottom that tells you how to reference files or other agents with the @ symbol, how to cancel a reply with the Esc key, and, only if you are on the free tier and have not yet linked your ChatGPT account, a reminder to run the /connect command so you can access the /plan and /review features. That conditional line appears exclusively for free-tier users who are currently disconnected from ChatGPT, and nothing changes for paid users or anyone who has already connected their account. This is already live today, along with several other unrelated tweaks to the command-line interface such as making the advertisement banner clickable and updating the Freebuff branding.

ai.title: CLI ad banner entire area clickable, info panel hidden
ai.summary: The ad banner's click target expands from discrete buttons to the entire content area, wrapped in a `Button` component. Hover states and click handlers now trigger on the whole banner. The expanded info panel is hidden by default, only appearing on specific interaction, while the 'Ad ?' label logic is gated by `IS_FREEBUFF`.

eli5.text: Clicking anywhere on the ad banner in the CLI now opens the linked website, instead of only clicking a specific text button. The extra info panel that used to pop up when you clicked the ad no longer appears by default, so the banner stays compact. The 'Ad ?' label that hints at the panel only shows up for non-free-tier CLI users, keeping the banner simpler for free users.

ai.title: Freebuff hides agent mode toggle
ai.summary: AgentModeToggle width reservation skips when IS_FREEBUFF. Freebuff lacks mode toggle, so estimatedToggleWidth returns 0. Affects cli/src/hooks/use-chat-input.ts. Prevents layout gap in Freebuff CLI.

eli5.text: When you use the Freebuff version of the assistant, you will no longer see an empty gap where a mode toggle used to be reserved. The assistant simply stops leaving that blank space because Freebuff never shows the toggle, so the layout now matches the rest of the interface instead of leaving a small unused strip.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.12 bundles Tips banner, clickable ad, and toggle hide
ai.summary: Freebuff 0.0.12 ships as a single-line version bump in freebuff/cli/release/package.json from 0.0.11 to 0.0.12. The release packages marketing copy updates moving the headline from 'strongest free coding agent' to 'free coding agent' across freebuff/README.md, freebuff/cli/release/README.md, and web/src/app/home-client.tsx. A new Tips section in the CLI help banner conditionally prompts /connect for /plan and /review access when ChatGPT OAuth is disconnected, while the agent mode toggle width reservation is skipped when IS_FREEBUFF to prevent layout gaps. The ad banner click target also expands from discrete buttons to the entire content area.
ai.evidence: The commit bumps the version field in freebuff/cli/release/package.json from 0.0.11 to 0.0.12. The bundled user-visible changes since 0.0.11 include marketing copy updates in freebuff/README.md and web/home-client.tsx, a Tips section with conditional /connect OAuth prompt in cli/src/components/help-banner.tsx, an entire-area clickable ad banner in the CLI, and hiding the agent mode toggle via IS_FREEBUFF in cli/src/hooks/use-chat-input.ts.

eli5.text: Freebuff's latest release makes the help screen more useful and the ad banner easier to interact with. The help area now includes a Tips section that offers quick pointers on useful features, and it can prompt you to connect your ChatGPT account if you're missing access to certain tools. The sponsored ad at the top of the chat is now fully clickable across its entire area, making it simpler to learn more about what's being advertised, while the detailed info panel is tucked away until you choose to open it. The agent mode toggle, which isn't used in Freebuff, is now hidden to keep the interface clean and avoid empty spaces. On the web and in documentation, the messaging has been updated to reflect current performance claims and new model options, giving users a more accurate picture of what Freebuff offers.

ai.title: Add shimmer subtitle to Freebuff CLI logo
ai.summary: Adds 'The free coding agent' subtitle with animated shimmer to the Freebuff CLI logo in cli/src/hooks/use-logo.tsx. Shimmer effect cycles through 10 steps at 180ms intervals, highlighting 'free' with theme-aware color gradients (base/bright/peak). Subtitle centering calculated via logo width parsing. Gated by IS_FREEBUFF constant. Scope: CLI logo hook only. Detail: Shimmer position drives per-character color selection with distance-based gradient logic.

eli5.text: When you open the Freebuff command-line coding tool, its startup logo now displays a short tagline, 'The free coding agent', right below the main logo text. The word 'free' in that tagline is animated: a shimmering highlight slides back and forth across those four letters, cycling smoothly about every couple of seconds. The shimmer color automatically matches whether your terminal is set to a dark or light color scheme, so it stays visible and looks consistent. This visual tweak only appears in the Freebuff version of the tool; other builds of the CLI are unaffected.

ai.title: NZ added to free mode allowed countries
ai.summary: Added 'NZ' to the FREE_MODE_ALLOWED_COUNTRIES set in web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/_post.ts. Enables free AI coding agent access for users connecting from New Zealand. Scope limited to the web API completions endpoint.

eli5.text: If you log in from New Zealand, you can now use the free AI coding agent on the web without entering a payment method. The product keeps a list of countries allowed to use that free tier, and New Zealand joined it today. You wouldn't see a new button or setting for it yourself; the change just quietly lets a New Zealand IP address start a free session instead of being turned away at the door.

ai.title: /interview command added to CLI
ai.summary: Added /interview slash command to CLI, enabling AI-driven spec generation. Uses buildInterviewPrompt to enforce multi-round ask_user tool interactions, preventing premature code changes. Files modified: command-registry.ts, prompt-builders.ts, router.ts, slash-commands.ts, input-modes.ts. New 'interview' input mode disables slash suggestions and blocks keyboard exit.

eli5.text: When you type /interview in the chat, the assistant will now pause and ask you a series of clarifying questions, using its built-in question-asking tool, before writing up a detailed plan document for you. It won’t start coding or editing anything until those questions are answered across at least three rounds, keeping the conversation focused on understanding your request rather than guessing. New Zealand users also gained access to free mode today, and the help screen now shows tips when OAuth sign-in is available.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.13 release packages shimmer logo, NZ access
ai.summary: Version 0.0.13 is released via a single-line bump in freebuff/cli/release/package.json, incrementing from 0.0.12. This patch packages three user-visible changes: a shimmer-animated 'The free coding agent' subtitle on the CLI logo, New Zealand ('NZ') added to the free mode allowed countries set, and a new /interview slash command with a dedicated interview input mode that drives spec generation through multi-round ask_user interactions. The shimmer effect runs at 180ms intervals across 10 steps with theme-aware per-character color gradients; the country addition scopes the web API completions endpoint; and /interview disables slash suggestions and blocks keyboard exit during the prompt flow.
ai.evidence: Diff hunk in freebuff/cli/release/package.json changes the version field from 0.0.12 to 0.0.13. This is a release-bump commit with a single modified file (freebuff/cli/release/package.json), +1/-1 stats, and the commit message 'Bump Freebuff version to 0.0.13'.

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.0.13 adds a sparkling animated logo tagline ('The free coding agent'), opens up free access for New Zealand users, and introduces a new /interview command that walks you through building a spec with AI before any code is written. The CLI startup now displays a shimmering subtitle beneath the logo, cycling animated colors across the word 'free', so the terminal greets you with a clearer brand message. New Zealand-based users can now connect to the web API and use the AI coding agent for free, expanding the regions where free mode is available. A new /interview slash command launches a guided, multi-round conversation mode that asks you questions to draft a project spec, blocking premature code edits and disabling keyboard shortcuts until the spec is complete, helping you think through requirements before building. Upgrading gives you a more inviting first-run experience, broader regional access, and a safer way to plan code through structured AI-guided interviews.

ai.title: Extract structured error details in SDK run
ai.summary: SDK run.ts now extracts structured error details from API response bodies. Parses responseBody for error code and message fields. Scope: sdk/src/run.ts. Handles AI_APICallError responseBody JSON parsing.

eli5.text: When the assistant runs into an error talking to the service behind the scenes, it will now read the detailed error message that the service sends back and show that specific message to you, instead of a generic technical error. This means if something goes wrong, like trying to use a feature that isn't available in your country, the error message you see will explain the actual problem in clearer terms. The improvement is live today and affects anyone using the assistant when it runs into certain backend errors. If you looked at the error output, you'd notice a more descriptive message and an error code that points to the specific issue.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI release bumped to 0.0.14
ai.summary: Release package version in freebuff/cli/release/package.json incremented from 0.0.13 to 0.0.14 as a standard patch release-bump. This accompanies the 0.0.14 release line and bundles the structured error detail extraction in sdk/src/run.ts shipped since 0.0.13.
ai.evidence: Commit 1a3128bb modifies freebuff/cli/release/package.json, changing the version field from 0.0.13 to 0.0.14 in the same-day release-bump sequence.

eli5.text: This release improves how the Freebuff CLI handles errors when something goes wrong with AI model calls. Now, when the CLI encounters a problem communicating with an AI service, it gives you clearer and more specific information about what failed and why. Instead of a vague error message, you get details like the exact error code and a human-readable explanation from the service. This makes it much easier to figure out whether the issue was a temporary service outage, an invalid request, or something else entirely. Upgrading to this version means fewer frustrating dead ends when AI calls fail, with just enough detail to help you (or support) quickly identify and fix the problem.

ai.title: New docs: architecture, error-schema, request-flow
ai.summary: Added three new documentation files: `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/error-schema.md`, and `docs/request-flow.md`. These documents detail the Codebuff monorepo structure, error handling mechanisms, and the end-to-end request flow from CLI to server and back. The architecture doc outlines package dependencies and responsibilities, the error-schema doc explains server responses and client-side transformation, and the request-flow doc traces the prompt lifecycle through SDK, agent runtime, and backend.

eli5.text: The Codebuff team added three new guidebooks to help anyone working on the software understand how the different parts fit together. One guide explains the overall structure of the project and how the pieces (CLI, SDK, agent engine, server) depend on each other. Another details how the server reports errors and how those errors get translated into friendly messages you see in the terminal. The third traces how your prompt travels from your terminal through the SDK and agent runtime to the server and back. These are reference documents only; they do not change what the software does today, but make it easier for developers to navigate the codebase.

ai.title: Extract API error codes and messages from response body
ai.summary: Added parseApiErrorResponseBody helper to extract structured error codes and messages from API response bodies. Agent runtime and SDK now use this helper to surface server-side error details (e.g., Forbidden) instead of generic error strings. AgentOutputSchema gains optional error field to carry parsed error codes. Covers common/src/util/error.ts, packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts, and sdk/src/run.ts.

eli5.text: Your assistant can now show you the real reason a request was denied. When your provider says 'no' (for example, 'Forbidden'), you will see that specific message and reason code in the response instead of a generic error. Behind the scenes, a new parser reads the server's JSON error reply and pulls out the machine-readable error code and human-readable message, and the assistant passes those details along so you get a clearer explanation of what went wrong.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI 0.0.15 release bump
ai.summary: Bumps the Freebuff CLI release version from 0.0.14 to 0.0.15 in freebuff/cli/release/package.json. The change is scoped exclusively to package metadata with no accompanying code changes, consistent with recent same-day release commits. This version ships the new architecture, error-schema, and request-flow documentation alongside structured API error extraction via parseApiErrorResponseBody, which surfaces server-side error codes through the agent runtime and SDK.
ai.evidence: Commit 86eb60f9 modifies freebuff/cli/release/package.json, incrementing the version field from 0.0.14 to 0.0.15. The diff is a single-line change on that field with no functional code modifications.

eli5.text: This release adds three new reference guides that explain how the system works behind the scenes, making it easier for developers and users to understand how commands flow through the application and how things get built and packaged. You now get clearer error messages when something goes wrong, because the system can read detailed explanations sent by the server instead of showing a generic message. The new documentation covers the overall structure of the application, the rules for how errors are reported and displayed, and the step-by-step path a request takes from your terminal all the way through to the backend and back. Upgrading gives you more transparency into what is happening when you use the tool, plus more helpful feedback when problems occur, so you can understand and fix issues faster.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI 1.0.631 release
ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI advances to version 1.0.631, bundling the React 19 upgrade, the CanopyWave then SiliconFlow then OpenRouter provider routing for MiniMax M2.5, Freebuff geo-restrictions to US/CA/NZ/GB/AU plus 12 European/Nordic countries, the ChatGPT OAuth /connect:chatgpt flow with local callback server, and the GPT-5.4 adoption across /plan and /review. Slash commands gained /interview for AI-driven spec generation with a new 'interview' input mode, while /review now spawns @thinker-gpt instead of @GPT-5 Agent. Additional Freebuff CLI polish includes a shimmer subtitle on the logo, an entire ad-banner click target, a Tips section in the help banner with conditional OAuth prompts, and the agent mode toggle hidden in Freebuff mode.
ai.evidence: cli/release/package.json: version field bumped from 1.0.630 to 1.0.631 (release-bump commit d31f9d4a, 2026-03-14). The release bundles 30+ changes across React 19 upgrade, CanopyWave/Fireworks/SiliconFlow provider routing, Freebuff geo-restrictions, OAuth /connect:chatgpt, /interview, /plan, /review, and GPT-5.4 adoption.

eli5.text: This release makes the Freebuff coding agent faster and smarter to use, adds a couple of new AI-powered commands, and broadens access so more regions can try it for free. You can now run /plan to kick off a ChatGPT-based planning session, and /review now uses a stronger thinker model instead of the previous one. The agent can connect your ChatGPT Pro subscription directly so you can tap higher-end models, and free users in more English-speaking countries (including New Zealand, Ireland, Norway, and 10 others) are now eligible instead of just the US and Canada. The MiniMax M2.5 model you see in the tool selector has been refreshed, and streaming chats route through a faster Fireworks backend with automatic fallbacks and smarter retry logic when demand spikes. Daily use is smoother too: the installer guide collapses into a quick copy-paste setup, the landing page copy is toned down from 'strongest' to 'free coding agent', and the help banner now surfaces tips like how to mention files and agents in chat. Finally, the CLI shows a shimmering 'The free coding agent' tagline under the logo and makes the entire ad banner clickable, keeping the experience clean while still surfacing first-party ads.
